Nine years ago, a curse spread across the land
Color vanished from the world, leaving only sorrow in its wake
No one living knows how it happened
But the curse continues to spread
If I were lucky, I would have shared my parents' fate
But my body refused to die
So I linger on in this wretched world
Watching the curse grow stronger day by day
I devoted my life to ending the nightmare but to no avail…
The rumors say it all began in this castle…
…and that none who enter are ever seen again.
After nine years, I am willing to take the risk,
even if it costs me my life.
After all, I've already lost everything else
With the source of the curse destroyed
After nine years, the shadows began to dispel
Talos and its inhabitants were freed from the darkness
Some still carried scars from the curse
When I came to this castle I barely cared if I lived or died
I just wanted to be free from the curse one way or another
I was just like you, Apino
I wanted to confront the darkness but I wasn't ready
We needed the journey we went on together
Part of me wishes that we could leave our sorrow behind
So the loss would never sting again
But we must carry it with us
The memories, painful though they are, tie us to the ones we loved
But the spell was too powerful. His very being was split: heart and body separated.
His heart, without a place to go, sought refuge in the closest object it could find:
His body, with all of its sorrow and pain still trapped inside,
was twisted into the demonic form of Belial,
Who wanders these halls in agony.
The very monster the ancient Dorians saw in their visions of the end of the world.
Was it wise to let that little ghost follow me?
Truthfully, I don’t think I'd get very far alone.
That demon I fought was stronger than any monster I've ever faced before.
I wonder if it's the source of the curse or if it was drawn to it...
She spoke as if she knew me.
And how are these so-called "relics" going to help me?
Everyone is placing too much hope in the wrong person…
So am I. With the power of the relics, maybe I can become powerful enough to face that demon again.
Claude seems to know more about this curse than he lets on. What is he hiding?
Of course Draythus is here. Just my luck.
Whatever he is searching for, it won't be good news if he finds it.
The last thing I need is his meddling.
Last time we fought I was clearly outmatched.
If he gets in my way, I'll have to duel him again.
With my luck, it's going to happen sooner rather than later.
What they say about this place is true...\n
The castle wasn't just built atop a sleeping giant, it's become part of him.
Whatever is down here is dangerous if it can pose a threat to Talos.
I hope it hasn't been completely consumed by darkness by the time I arrive.
Surely the castle would have collapsed if it had already happened...
The only thing I ever needed to do was kill that damned ghost.
And now I've helped him become stronger!
Every time I trust someone in this gods-forsaken world, I get burned.
The worst part is that without him, there's not much I can do to avoid the demon. At least... not for long.
What am I going to do?
This place is making me nervous. It's getting more dangerous all the time.\n
It's impressive how long Talos has resisted…
Even after all this time, the people out there remain oblivious to the danger they are in.
I can't even imagine what would happen if the curse spread throughout the rest of the world.
I wonder what my parents would think of me now.\n
Would I seem brave to them? Reckless? Desperate?
I'd like to think they would be proud.
Any bravery I have came from them.
My arms and knees are starting to ache.
Running around this castle is taking a toll on me. \n
There's no time for weakness, but I wish I could catch my breath.
Playing the piano again was... nice.
I hadn't played since my mother's last birthday.
I had forgotten what it felt like.
It takes me back to that moment. Comforting her with music in her last moments.
It's as if I can still hear her trying to sing along...
The armor I have found is incredible...
Whoever created it was a master of their craft.
It would be dangerous for it to fall into the wrong hands.
I wonder what happened to all those brave souls who came here before me.
Could they still be here? Fighting?\n
Maybe I'll cross paths with one.
Or maybe they all died trying to do the same thing as me.
I recall my father speaking of the skills of master blacksmiths, but none of them sound like Master Hibino.
I wonder where he learned his craft.
Perhaps it was a divine gift he was born with.
If the first knights that entered Talos had received his help, could the curse have been stopped sooner?
I remember the day I received my dress and halberd.
I wanted to do something with them. I wanted to accomplish something.
I wanted to honor my parents.
I never could have imagined it, at least not at the time.
But now it seems... as if it was always meant to be.
This castle seems like the last place I'd start meeting people...
Yet now may be as good a time as any to start...
…just to have someone who can remember me when I'm gone.
What a glorious place this castle must have been before the curse.
All these beautiful hallways and windows...
...the detailed engravings with centuries of history…
And now they are just withering away.\n
This place deserved a better fate.
I wish I could sleep at night the way I used to.
I miss my home... my bed...
I felt so safe within those walls.
The warmth of the fireplace and its gentle light...
And my mother singing me to sleep...\n

One origin, one purpose: Host to the ancient civilizations. Bearer of the great shrines, whose mighty tribes have perished. Amfibis Pethiko Capra "Preserve, preserve. You are a fortress." Beyond the end of the ancients came the nations: The second genesis, the new burdens. Upon my back, I bore home and sanctuary from time beyond memory to the day of darkness.

The universe was born from a sacred spell. Healing, divine magic: Music. And so is the theater the greatest of rooms, where art—and by it, life—is born. Few have stood among the Great Composers, noble guides and healers sent by the gods. As long as music fills my theater my heart and mind shall know peace.

From the ocean depths
arose a mystical tribe.

Amfibis—the lovers of beauty,
protectors of hopes and dreams,
steadfast in times of uncertainty.

From their hands were born the rivers and waterfalls,
which flow as lifeblood within me.

Their prayers echoed in my bones:
"Protect us, divine guardian,
from the grasp of the serpent."

Loyal Amfibis:
Souls pure as spring water.
Beings of harmony.

Pethiko—the most valiant of warriors, who sang as one to cleanse themselves of despair. Their tunnels stretched from sky to earth as my veins, through which they traveled, under the piercing watch of the many-eyed bird whose gaze they fled. Agile, intelligent, fertile. Defenders. Lovers of nature. At home among trees.

Not long ago the new kingdom upon my back a stronghold laid. The warmth of life began to hum so I and castle a union made. Within my hallways dwelt the young with hope and sadness mixed in song. One bore a deep, lasting sorrow. Arms raised high, he stole away. His weeping before daylight stirred. Stained bright moon and stilled blessed word. The shadows claimed my inner flame. The curse's triumph now made claim, to blackened sun at hollow dawn. In Talos now made Abaddon.

From the mountains came the Capra:
the strong and clever machinists
with their cauldrons and furnaces.

They built spiderwebs of pipes and gears,
slung throughout my great heart, 
blasting the steam that became my pulse.
They warned of the untamable
Flame of Demise, as they labored.

Through their example
I learned of honor and duty.

Their hearts certain, their voices sure,
Your only task: endure.


The ancient people toiled as one,
My body the proof of their union.
Their hope and love for this old world
gave purpose to the plan they spun.


"You must contain the curse!" they cried.
I heed their words.
I will comply,
until my last wall turns to dust.

I can feel it...
In every corner, every crevice...
It spreads—this cursed plague.
It hardens my heart,
devouring the light,
and stiffening the beats.

I am metal, and I am stone.
But I am more.
I swore an oath,
I will not waver,
I will not break.

I am a witness.
I remember, for I have seen


Kingdoms
Wars
Festivals
Deaths
Dawns
Defeats


The seasons change while years repeat,
and always live the memories:
The dance, the blood, the rise, and fall.
This I know, for I have seen it all.

It arrived.
An absent moon.
The darkness from lighted past foreseen.


Where is the warrior?
Why the silence upon my stage?
Away, away, they abandon me.
Run! Run! The little ones fear
the colorless night of darkness near.


Your only task: endure




They have left me.

The guardian of the gates of the afterlife. He will not allow anyone to desecrate the land of the dead.
An expert game player, he spent a lifetime designing a machine that would allow him to use chess pieces to defeat his opponents. Winning has never been so crucial.

A monster born from shadows and dread. Bringer of the curse, chaos, and destruction. Cold fear emanates from its hollow chest, filling even the bravest warriors with horror. Although many have tried, none have been able to defeat it.
The 'Many-Eyed Bird" described by the Pethiko people is a violent and erratic beast. Its body is covered in metallic feathers that conceal countless crystals of darkness.

A ruthless bounty hunter with a mysterious connection to the castle of Talos. He embarked on a journey to singlehandedly stop the curse, but was corrupted by the darkness, leaving only a small shred of his humanity intact.

A recurrent nightmare that is summoned every thunderous night to steal the souls of the hopeless. No one knows why or how, but once its piercing gaze finds a victim, they finally learn the true meaning of fear.

Once a symbol of prosperity, the Flame Keeper witnessed the decline and collapse of everything it held dear. In its grief, it descended into madness and became the visage of demise, casting a pall of misery onto any who draw near.

A mechanical creature that predated the curse, quietly contributing its energy to help power the mechanisms within the castle. After the curse corrupted it, it weaponized its energy generating abilities.

A creature of deceit that was once a devout worshiper of a long-forgotten entity. Without the object of its reverence, it was consumed by despair and hid its true form. Now it is lost to the shadows, and it attempts to slay any who cross its path.
Once a peaceful creature, it grew in solitude for generations. Despite its imposing size and power, it was never a menace to Talos until the day the corruption finally reached its heart.

Raging serpents that were once a symbol of hope. Now they slither in the depths of the Forgotten Pond, threatening all living things within it. The Amfibis tribe narrowly avoided them and found a home in the shallower waters.

Hidden deep within the castle, the Heart of Talos beats in anguish as it struggles to maintain the lifeforce of the giant. While many parts of Talos emulate machinery, this vital organ hints at the organic nature of Talos: a being capable of dying. It beats on, waiting with dim hope of rescue.
